title: Release Rust Helper v0.4.0
description: Ship the active Rust build monitor as v0.4.0 after clearing CI, validating locally and remotely, tagging the release, verifying cross-platform assets, publishing the GitHub release, and confirming the Homebrew update workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Main CI succeeds; v0.4.0 tag builds signed release assets for all configured platforms; GitHub release is published; Homebrew update workflow succeeds; local main is pushed and matches origin.

title: Rust Helper - Multi-project Rust management Tauri app
description: A macOS Tauri app to manage multiple Rust projects from ~/Workspace. Features include auto-discover and scan Rust projects, clean build artifacts, check outdated dependencies, security audits, health checks (fmt/clippy/test), and dependency analysis across projects.

title: Monitor and control active Rust build processes
description: Add a live app view that discovers currently running Cargo/Rust build processes across the system, shows project and resource/progress signals, and provides guarded stop and restart controls.
acceptance_criteria: The app automatically refreshes active Rust build processes; each process shows command, project/cwd, elapsed time, CPU/memory, state, and subprocess count; users can stop or restart a build with confirmation and inline errors; backend process parsing and control behavior are covered by tests.
notes: Implemented system-wide Cargo/rustc process discovery with phase/resource aggregation, 2.5s UI refresh, guarded tree-aware stop/restart, PID reuse and self-ancestry protection, responsive Builds view, and inline errors. Validated with 112 Rust tests, npm production build, cargo fmt, normal Clippy, and representative 800x600 visual QA. Strict Clippy remains blocked only by legacy warnings tracked in rust-helper-8h5.12.
close_reason: Feature implemented and validated; legacy Clippy cleanup split to rust-helper-8h5.12.

title: Clear legacy Clippy warnings in command module
description: The build-process monitor work ran Clippy with -D warnings and found seven pre-existing warnings in src-tauri/src/commands/mod.rs: unnecessary sort_by usage and redundant into_iter calls. Normal Clippy succeeds, but the strict warning-free gate remains blocked until these are cleaned up.
acceptance_criteria: cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings succeeds without changing command behavior.
close_reason: Replaced Clippy-flagged sort and iterator patterns; strict all-target/all-feature Clippy, 112 Rust tests, frontend build, and formatting now pass.
